obligation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (benchmark)
basis: No sector cybersecurity rule binds a temporary help firm (NAICS 561320), so CSF 2.0 is the program benchmark (label N56-BM); the firm measures itself against its own target profile

obligation: FTC/FACTA Disposal Rule
basis: The firm procures about 190,000 consumer reports a year for employment purposes and keeps consumer report information in SYS-02 and the screening portals (682.3 applies to any person that maintains or possesses it for a business purpose)

obligation: FCRA employment background checks
basis: The firm procures consumer reports for employment purposes through two consumer reporting agencies, so the disclosure, authorization and adverse action duties apply

obligation: Form I-9 retention, inspection and electronic I-9 standards
basis: Employer of record for associates; completes their Forms I-9 in an electronic I-9 system (SYS-02) and keeps a scanned paper archive. For direct-hire referrals and RPO the hiring client completes the Form I-9

obligation: HIPAA (as business associate)
basis: A business associate acts other than as a member of the covered entity's workforce (45 CFR 160.103). Travel and per diem clinicians work under the hospital's direct control, so they are the hospital's workforce, and the firm does not handle PHI on a hospital's behalf. The 37 hospital BAAs are contractual commitments (see CONTRACT-BAA). Employee group health plans are separate covered entities outside scope

obligation: TCPA / Telemarketing Sales Rule
basis: The TSR does not apply (the firm does not telemarket goods or services). TCPA consent rules reach automated recruiting texts, a contact-consent duty run by the Privacy Office, not a security duty

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1
basis: The firm accepts no payment cards (clients pay by ACH or wire); paycards are issued and run by a bank program manager

obligation: FAR Basic Safeguarding clause
basis: 34 federal contracts carry the clause, and federal contract information (agency timesheets, invoices, contract reports) is in SYS-01 and SYS-03. No CUI is handled, so DFARS 252.204-7012 and NIST SP 800-171 do not apply. Awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation carry FAR 52.240-93 with the same 15 requirements

obligation: NYC Local Law 144 (Automated Employment Decision Tools)
basis: The firm is an employment agency using AI-001 to rank candidates for jobs at 9 NYC branches

obligation: PHMSA hazmat security plans
basis: The firm neither offers nor transports hazardous materials

obligation: E-Verify MOU for Employers and the FAR E-Verify clause
citation: E-Verify MOU Art. II.A and II.B; 48 CFR 52.222-54
basis: The firm signed the MOU for Employers and, because Government Solutions holds federal contracts with the FAR E-Verify clause, is enrolled as a Federal contractor; it verifies all new hires in every state

obligation: Florida E-Verify law (worked example of state E-Verify laws)
basis: Private employer with 25 or more employees in Florida (448.095(2)(b)2.); other states' E-Verify laws are met by the same enterprise process

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106
basis: Same registrant status; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over the payroll engine and ERP are tested by the SOX program and not repeated here

obligation: Title VII, ADA and ADEA for AI selection procedures
basis: The firm is an employer and an employment agency, and AI-001 and AI-009 rank people for work

obligation: Colorado automated decision-making technology law
citation: C.R.S. 6-1-1701 to 6-1-1709 as reenacted by SB26-189
basis: The firm does business in Colorado and uses AI-001 in employment decisions about Colorado applicants; the law applies to consequential decisions made on or after 2027-01-01, and no employee-count exemption appears in the signed act

obligation: California CPPA regulations (ADMT, risk assessments, cybersecurity audits)
basis: The firm is a CCPA business (annual gross revenue above $26,625,000) and holds sensitive personal information of more than 50,000 California consumers; ADMT duties apply to AI-001 from 2027-01-01, risk assessments for existing processing by 2027-12-31, and the first cybersecurity audit covers 2027

obligation: California Civil Rights Council automated-decision system regulations
basis: FEHA employer using an automated-decision system for California applicants; effective 2025-10-01

obligation: Illinois Public Act 103-0804 (AI in employment)
basis: Illinois employer using AI in hiring; effective 2026-01-01; IDHR rules pending

obligation: Connecticut Public Act 26-15 (notice of AI in employment decisions)
applies: Likely yes (effective 2026-10-01); text being confirmed by counsel
basis: The firm employs and recruits in Connecticut; only the Attorney General's release has been read

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification and reasonable measures; worked example)
basis: The firm holds personal information of Florida residents (headquarters, 61 branches, about 9,800 associates a week). Florida is the worked example for state law

obligation: Breach notification and data security laws of the other states
citation: Statutes of each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Associates and candidates live in every state; notify under the law of each state of residence, using outside counsel's state matrix

obligation: Florida Digital Bill of Rights
basis: A controller must exceed $1 billion in revenue and meet one of three activity tests (online advertising revenue, a smart speaker service or an app store); the firm meets the revenue test but none of the activity tests

obligation: State biometric privacy laws
citation: Statutes of the states where candidates and associates reside
basis: The time clock face-match feature is turned off at every site pending legal review (not analyzed here); the AI-007 identity verification pilot, registered after intake, handles face templates as biometric data and excludes Illinois candidates

obligation: FAR covered telecommunications, Kaspersky and FASCSA clauses
citation: FAR 52.204-23; 52.204-25; 52.204-30; FAR 52.240-91 under a FAR Part 40 class deviation
applies: Yes, for contracts that include the clauses
basis: Government Solutions federal contracts; a report is due only if a covered article is found

obligation: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act
basis: Final rule not published at intake; reporting to CISA is voluntary until it takes effect. Rechecked in P03 and P08

obligation: Sanctions screening before any extortion payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the cyber policy also requires insurer approval before any ransom payment

obligation: IRS Form W-2 and SSN data loss reporting
citation: IRS guidance for businesses and payroll service providers
basis: The payroll engine holds W-2 and SSN data for associates

obligation: Client agreements for SL-1 and SL-2 (availability, pay timeliness, notice and assurance terms)
citation: SL-1 client agreements; SL-2 payrolling agreements
basis: SL-1 clients are committed 99.9% monthly availability and receive an annual SOC 2 Type 2 report; SL-2 agreements commit on-time pay and accurate client reports, and clients ask for a SOC 2 Type 2

obligation: Hospital staffing agreements with business associate agreements
basis: Confidentiality and incident notice to the hospital client under the contract, not a HIPAA business associate determination

obligation: Client master services agreements and federal and state agency contracts (incident notice terms)
basis: Large clients commonly require notice within 72 hours; agency contracts set their own incident clauses

obligation: Bank, paycard program and cyber insurance agreements
citation: Cash management agreements; paycard program agreement; cyber policy
basis: Notice and cooperation terms with Banks A and B, the paycard program manager and the cyber insurer
